newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Britain to consider cancelling Zimbabwe debt.
newsitem.headline: Britain to consider cancelling Zimbabwe debt.

text.p: Britain would consider cancelling Zimbabwe's short-term debt of about Z$288 million (US$25.4 million) if the country came up with a second plan of action for economic reform, the state-owned Herald newspaper said on Tuesday.

It quoted Zimbabwe Minister of Finance Herbert Murerwa as saying that during bilateral talks in London last week the British government had pledged to support Zimbabwe's privatisation and indigenisation process.

"We discussed the possibility of cancelling our debt and they indicated they are willing to consider it on condition we have a programme for the second phase of the reform programme," said Murerwa, who had met Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke.
The paper said the short-term debt amounted to about Z$288 million.

The second phase of reforms, titled the Zimbabwe Programme for Economic and Social Transformation, would be launched this year once the consultation process in government and with industry and labour had been completed.
